p
For years, "SaaS" meant software as a service. You paid every month for a tool. Then you sat down and did the work with it.
That is changing. The new deal is the other way round: **service as software.** You pay for the work, and the software does it.
h2
The old deal: a tool and a to-do list
the-old-deal-a-tool-and-a-to-do-list

Think about what a business had to do to show up on social media. Somebody had to come up with the idea. Somebody had to write the script. Somebody had to film it, cut it, add captions, pick the music and size it for each platform. Then somebody had to write the caption, post it, and do it all again tomorrow.

The software helped with each step. A video editor gave you a timeline. A design app gave you a blank canvas. A scheduler gave you a calendar. Every one of them was a tool, and every one of them waited for you.

So you had two choices. Do it yourself, at night, after the real work. Or hire it out: a videographer to film, an editor to cut, a social media manager to plan and post. That is three people, three invoices and a lot of back-and-forth before one reel goes out.
The new deal: you ask, it does the work
the-new-deal-you-ask-it-does-the-work
Service as software means the software does the job those people did. You do not learn it. You tell it what you want.

In VEXI that happens in a chat. Type what you want the way you would say it to a person: "a reel for our weekend special," "three posts about the new menu," "a script for a 30-second video about our return policy." It comes back finished.
Start from a photo, a clip, a link, or nothing at all. **You do not need editing skills.** The chat shows its progress as it works.
What the work looks like now
what-the-work-looks-like-now
Here is the work a business used to do itself or hire out, and what happens to it now.
**The writing.** Tell it what the script should do and it writes it. It writes the captions too, in the way you write. If you want to be on camera, your script rolls on screen while you record.

**The editing.** Videos come back cut, with B-roll and captions, sized for each platform. Upload a long raw recording, like a podcast, and get back the clips that work best, captioned, with music laid under each cut. That was the editor's job.

**The design.** Posts come back with your logo, colors, fonts and voice applied every time. To change something, tap it on the design: the headline, the photo, the logo, the colors. No layers and no export settings.
**The posting.** Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and your Google Business Profile, posted for you. That was the social media manager's job.
And if it gets something wrong? Say what you wanted instead and it remakes it. With approvals on, nothing goes out until you are happy with it.
Autopilot is where it becomes a service
autopilot-is-where-it-becomes-a-service
Making one post on request is useful. But a service does not wait to be asked every day. It keeps going.

That is what the AI Autopilot does. Switch it on, and it fills your week ahead with posts and videos. It posts at the times your audience actually shows up. One control sets how designed the posts should look, and it holds that mix.
You decide how much to hand over. Autopilot can wait for your approval on everything, or run on its own and post at the times that perform. Check the week when you feel like it.
This is the part that used to need a person on staff. Somebody who remembers to post on Tuesday, plans next week, and keeps it going when you are busy. Now that is the software.
What it does not change
what-it-does-not-change

You still know your business better than any software does. The offer, the story and the reason clients come back are yours. Service as software does not replace that. It replaces the hours between having the idea and seeing it posted.
It also does not ask you to become a video editor, a designer or a social media manager. That was the old deal. The new one is simple: say what you want, check it if you like, and let it run.
